title: Asian markets follow Wall Street: Nikkei, Kospi jump up to 8% as Jensen Huang’s return sparks rally in AI stocks | Stock Market News
text:
Asian equities staged a powerful rebound on Tuesday, 24 November, tracking a sharp rally on Wall Street as renewed optimism around the artificial intelligence (AI) trade lifted technology stocks. Nvidia's spectacular surge helped restore confidence among investors after a turbulent week for global AI-linked shares. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan jumped 4.6%, recovering from an eight-month low and heading for its biggest single-day advance in two weeks. Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 4.5% as trading resumed after a local market holiday. South Korea's KOSPI rallied 7.5%, while Taiwan's benchmark index soared 9.1%, reflecting the strong recovery in technology-heavy markets. The gains followed an extraordinary session on Wall Street, where Nvidia shares soared 31.5% on Monday. According to Reuters, this was the chipmaker's biggest one-day percentage gain in 23 years, adding nearly $1 trillion to its market value. The sharp rebound in Nvidia shares provided a major boost to the broader technology sector, easing concerns that had weighed on the AI trade in recent sessions. Nvidia's influence extends well beyond chip supplies. The company has also played a significant role in financing the AI industry's expansion, making its performance a key barometer of investor confidence in the sector. The Nasdaq 100, which has significant exposure to large technology companies, jumped more than 6% on Monday. The S&P 500 gained 4.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%. Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, told Reuters that the return of the AI industry's most influential figure to the leadership of its most important company had eased some of the uncertainty surrounding the AI trade. However, concerns about a potential slowdown in AI investments and moderating earnings growth have not disappeared, he cautioned. Despite the technology-led recovery, uncertainty over the US interest rate outlook continues to pose a challenge for global markets. Investors are weighing expectations of tighter Federal Reserve policy, which have lifted US Treasury yields and supported the dollar. The changing rate outlook could influence risk appetite across global equity markets even as technology stocks recover. Market participants are now looking ahead to Wednesday's US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index data, a key inflation measure, for clues about the Federal Reserve's policy direction ahead of its final meeting of 2026. Rodda also highlighted the importance of the upcoming inflation data, noting that uncertainty around US monetary policy remains another risk for markets. The sharp gains on Monday provided a strong boost to global investor sentiment, although early trading in US equity futures suggested some caution. S&P 500 futures were largely unchanged early on Tuesday, while Nasdaq futures slipped 0.2%, indicating that investors were assessing the sustainability of the previous session's rally. For now, Nvidia's surge has helped calm nerves across the AI ecosystem and triggered a broad recovery in Asian technology stocks. However, the outlook for AI spending, corporate earnings and US interest rates will remain central to the market's next move. Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only.
